key_insight: Faster code is not automatically greener: energy savings during execution must also cover the energy spent on LLM-driven optimization. The paper evaluates this trade-off, but the provided abstract is truncated and does not report results.
problem_solved: How can developers determine whether iterative LLM-based performance optimization actually reduces total energy use compared with canonical human-written reference solutions?
method: Use iterative LLM self-refinement to generate performance-optimized code.
Measure optimized code’s execution energy relative to canonical human reference solutions.
Assess whether subsequent execution savings can offset the energy cost of the optimization process.
impact: AI/ML practitioners should evaluate optimization overhead alongside runtime improvements. A net-energy perspective can help determine when LLM-based code optimization is worth deploying.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: reference code → iterative LLM optimization → optimized code → energy evaluation.
Paired speedometer and energy-meter icons to distinguish execution speed from energy consumption.
Stacked energy bars separating optimization overhead from cumulative execution energy.
Conceptual break-even chart showing total energy versus number of executions.
paper_title: Green Code or Costly Code? Evaluating the Energy Costs of Iterative LLM-Based Code Optimizations
paper_authors: Sadra Emami, Benjamin Weigell, Mohammad Reza Mousavi, Gunel Jahangirova, Hugo Araujo
